question: Should this PR land the broad Codex Computer Use fail-closed readiness defaults, symlinked cache reconciliation, periodic health/repair, lease surface, fallback policy, and direct MCP probe exception as-is, or should it be narrowed first?
rationale: The branch changes setup/startup defaults, host filesystem cache behavior, host process cleanup, and a sandbox-adjacent app-server boundary; those are maintainer product and security-boundary choices rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Keep the live readiness/cache fix but minimize new default/config surface and require explicit owner approval for the MCP exception and repair behavior.

options.title: Accept Broad Defaults
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the compatibility and security-boundary impact if the new defaults are the desired product direction.

options.title: Split The Branch
options.body: Separate readiness probing, cache reconciliation, health/repair, leases, and docs/config into smaller owner-reviewed PRs if this combined branch is too broad.

recommendation.title: Narrow Before Merge
recommendation.body: Keep the live readiness/cache fix but minimize new default/config surface and require explicit owner approval for the MCP exception and repair behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent local history across the current Codex app-server, config, sandbox guard, and docs surfaces touched by this decision.
